citation: Li et al., MAGE: Machine-generated Text Detection in the Wild, arXiv:2305.13242.

detector.operating_point: native categorical verdict; no score threshold; no calibration

licence.licence: Apache-2.0 (LICENSE file, repo metadata, HF tag); README badge asserts CC BY 4.0 — record both, attribute the authors
licence.licence_note: Verified 2026-11-06: LICENSE file, GitHub metadata and HF API tag all say Apache-2.0, but the README licence badge reads CC BY 4.0. Both readings are permissive (no NC/ND/research-only restriction), so local evaluation is permitted under either; attribute the MAGE authors in any case. Upstream caveat as with RAID: human texts come from 10 source datasets whose own licences are not stated.
licence.permitted_use: local non-commercial evaluation only; no redistribution; no raw text in the repo
licence.reverified: 2026-11-16 (live: HF API cardData + GitHub repo metadata)

near_duplicate_check.note: MAGE source_id is the first 16 hex of the text SHA-256, so content-hash disjointness (0 shared samples) is source disjointness; no separate near-duplicate pass applies.

final_test.shift_rule: unshifted strided grid; no prior test-split sample exists

partitions.note: train/dev/selection/fit are EMPTY BY DESIGN: no threshold, calibration or selection decision is made from any data; the detector's operating point is fixed by the detector itself.
